notification.currency.title: No base currency: nothing is computed
notification.currency.body: Your events are recorded. Nothing is valued and no gain or rate is computed until you choose a base currency.
notification.fact.assumed_base_currency: Amounts read in your base currency
notification.advisory.cash_share.body: Part of this account is sitting in cash rather than being invested. Nothing is wrong with that if it is deliberate.
empty.noCurrency.title: No base currency yet
empty.noCurrency.body: Nothing is valued and no gain is computed until you choose a base currency. Your events are recorded all the same, and the ledger stays readable.
empty.unread.title: This could not be read
notFound.title: No such page
absence.noQuote: {count, plural, one {# consecutive reading, no price} other {# consecutive readings, no price}}
dashboard.gainTotal.explain: Everything your portfolio has earned: unrealised gain, realised gain, dividends received, and the fees your broker takes on transfers. The four add up to this total.
dashboard.ytd.pending: history not rebuilt that far back yet
dashboard.netContributed.explain: Your deposits less your withdrawals, fees excluded. Both returns are measured against it.
dashboard.xirr.explain: What your deposits actually earned, as a yearly rate. It takes the date of every deposit and withdrawal into account, so money paid in before a rise counts more than money paid in after it.
dashboard.twr.explain: How your holdings themselves performed, whatever you paid in or took out. That is what makes two portfolios of different sizes comparable. It depends on the period shown, so read it with that period.
dashboard.awaitingCurrency: Your total value, your net contributed and both returns are waiting for a base currency.
dashboard.withoutLedger: Record your deposits and withdrawals to see your total value, your net contributed and both returns.
dashboard.empty.title: No events yet
dashboard.empty.body: Everything here is computed from your events: purchases, sales, dividends, deposits. You have not recorded any yet.
dashboard.chart.empty: Nothing to draw over this range yet.
dashboard.movers.title: Movers
dashboard.movers.others: {count, plural, one {# other holding is} other {# other holdings are}} not shown here, {unchanged, plural, =0 {none of which moved by nothing} one {# of which moved by nothing} other {# of which moved by nothing}}.
dashboard.movers.empty.body: A holding appears here once it has a price on two sessions.
dashboard.accounts.title: Your accounts, compared
dashboard.accounts.empty: Nothing to compare over this range yet.
installation.rebuild.title: Rebuilding your history
installation.rebuild.body: Your history is being rebuilt. Prices are still being read; the consolidated figures are catching up.
installation.rebuild.body.account: Your history is being rebuilt. {account} is furthest behind, and the consolidated figures are waiting for it.
installation.rebuild.progress: {percent, number, percent} of the period covered
currency.suggested: Suggested from your browser. Check that it matches your portfolio.
currency.untilAnswered: Once chosen it is fixed: every amount is recorded in it from then on, and changing it later would reinterpret them instead of converting them. You can answer whenever you like — you just cannot answer twice.
currency.fixed: Fixed: your amounts are recorded in this currency and it can no longer change.
firstRun.title: Welcome to SuiviBourse
firstRun.what.ledger: You record what you bought and sold: the security, the date, the price.
firstRun.what.quotes: SuiviBourse fetches the quotes by itself and works out the rest.
firstRun.what.walk: Three passages to get started: nothing is required, and all of it can be done later.
firstRun.ephemeral: This container keeps nothing: the store is inside it and disappears the next time it is recreated. Fine for trying the app out — mount a volume to keep your data.
firstRun.refused: The app refused this value and wrote nothing.
firstRun.pass.settings.title: Your reporting currency
firstRun.pass.settings.body: Choose the currency all your amounts are shown in. You can answer later, but once saved it cannot be changed.
firstRun.pass.accounts.title: Your accounts
firstRun.pass.accounts.body: Every event belongs to an account, and you already have one: you can walk past. If you already know how your holdings are split, declare your accounts now — otherwise the Accounts page is there for it.
firstRun.pass.events.title: Your first events
firstRun.pass.events.body: Two ways to start: import a file, or type an event by hand. You can also start empty and come back whenever you want.

shares.allocation.title: Allocation

shares.allocation.unplaced: {count, plural, one {# holding is} other {# holdings are}} not in this allocation, quoted with no rate yet: {symbols}. Including it would make every other percentage wrong.
shares.allocation.empty.body: You hold no open position, so there is nothing to split.
shares.head.title: Open lines · totals
shares.unrealised.explain: What a position is worth today less what it cost you. It moves with the market and it is not money you have yet. A position with no price is counted at its cost, so it shows zero.
shares.realised.explain: What your sales brought in, net of their fees and of the cost of the shares sold. The proceeds are already in your cash.
shares.dividends.explain: Dividends received on this position, fees already deducted. A position keeps this figure after you sell it.
shares.avgCost.explain: The average price you paid for the shares you still hold, fees included. Selling does not change it, so a position you have closed has none.
shares.anomaly.count: {count, plural, =0 {No share needs attention} one {# share needs attention} other {# shares need attention}}
shares.anomaly.repair: No price was received for this share. Check the symbol — it is usually a typo.
shares.table.label: Held positions
shares.closed.label: Closed positions
shares.closed.toggle: {count, plural, one {# closed position} other {# closed positions}}
shares.empty.title: No positions
shares.empty.body: This page is computed from your events: purchases, sales, dividends. You have not recorded any yet.
shares.reduced: Reduced to account {account}. The figures above cover its lines alone.
shares.reduced.empty.title: No position on this account
shares.reduced.empty.body: Nothing in your ledger names a security held on {account}.
shares.sheet.gainNote: {known, select, yes {Unrealised, realised and dividends together · {percent} of what was put in} other {Unrealised, realised and dividends together}}

shares.chart.empty: No price recorded over this range.
shares.sheet.gainTotal.explain: The gain of this share alone: unrealised, realised and dividends. The three figures below add up to it.
shares.events.title: Events
shares.events.empty: No event recorded for this share.
shares.events.marker: {count, plural, one {# event on {date}} other {# events on {date}}}
shares.breakdown.title: By account

shares.fundamentals.title: The security

accounts.rail.title: Weight of your accounts
accounts.rail.label: Your accounts
accounts.xirr.explain: What your deposits into this account earned, as a yearly rate. It takes the date of every deposit and withdrawal into account.
accounts.totalPerformance.explain: This account’s whole gain divided by what you have paid into it — what a euro left here since the start has become. It covers the account’s entire life, so it is not a yearly rate.
accounts.reason.withoutCashLedger: no cash movement recorded on this account
accounts.default.label: Unassigned
accounts.default.reassign: Assign these events to an account
accounts.detail.gainTotal.explain: What this account is worth less what you have paid into it. It counts this account's sold positions, and only the fees taken on its own transfers.
accounts.detail.curve.title: Value against what you have paid in
accounts.detail.dividends.explain: What this account has actually paid you in cash, sold positions included — a share you sold keeps the dividends it paid while you held it.
accounts.detail.curve.period: Drawn over this account’s whole history
accounts.detail.lines.link: {count, plural, one {See this account’s line on Shares} other {See this account’s # lines on Shares}}
accounts.detail.events.link: See this account’s events in the ledger
accounts.remove.title: Remove this account
accounts.remove.offered: No event names this account, so removing it takes nothing with it. It cannot be undone from the app.
accounts.remove.seeded: This is the account every install has: every event naming no other is recorded there. Rename it rather than remove it.
accounts.remove.namedByEvents: {count, plural, one {# event names this account} other {# events name this account}}, so it cannot be removed — the events would point at nothing. Move them to another account, or delete them first.
accounts.reassign.title: Events assigned to no account
accounts.reassign.body: {count, plural, one {# event was recorded before you declared anything, so it names none of your accounts.} other {# events were recorded before you declared anything, so they name none of your accounts.}} Move them to one of your accounts. Your files are fine as they are — the app changed the rule under them.
accounts.form.reassign: {count, plural, one {Assign the # event that names no account to it} other {Assign the # events that name no account to it}}
accounts.form.reassign.hint: They were recorded before you declared anything, so they carry the account every installation starts with. Now is the time to move them: once imported, an event keeps the account it names.
accounts.form.create.title: A new account
accounts.form.edit.title: This account
accounts.form.description: An account is where your events are recorded, and you choose its name. It has no currency of its own — every figure in the app is shown in one currency.
accounts.form.id.fixed: This is what your events name, in a file as well as here, so it cannot be changed. Declare another account and move the events onto it instead.
accounts.form.id.hint: This is what your events name. It will not change.
accounts.form.type.hint: What you call it: PEA, brokerage, life insurance…
accounts.form.label: Name
accounts.empty.title: No account declared
accounts.empty.body: Every installation has one account, so this screen means the declaration could not be read — not that you have none. Declare one here: this is the only place an account is created.

data.filter.symbols: Reduced to {count, plural, one {one security} other {# securities}}: {symbols}

data.filter.none.title: No event matches
data.filter.none.body: Nothing you have recorded answers this search. Widen it, or clear the filters.
data.row.delete.title: Delete this event?
data.row.delete.body: {type} · {what} · {date}. It leaves the ledger, and everything derived from it — positions, average cost, gains, rates — is recomputed without it.
data.form.create.title: A new event
data.form.edit.title: This event
data.form.description: Say what happened, when, and for how much.
data.form.date.explain: Both returns are computed from these dates. If you no longer have the exact one, record your best estimate.
data.form.date.unreadable: Without a readable date nothing is recorded. Write it as YYYY-MM-DD.
data.form.account.unassigned: You have declared no account, so this event is recorded there — as every event that names none is. Declare one below the ledger to sort them.
data.form.account.pending: The list of your accounts has not arrived yet.
data.form.account.failed: Your accounts could not be read, so there is nothing to choose from here.
data.form.grantPrice.explain: Leave it empty and the award only adds shares — nothing paid in, nothing it cost you. Fill it and the shares enter your contributions and your cost basis, so the position starts with no unrealised gain.
data.form.required: This kind of event needs this field.
data.empty.file.title: Import a file
data.empty.file.body: Hand the app a .csv or .xlsx of your events. It reads it once, whatever it is called — a file covering a single year is a fine start.
data.empty.manual.title: Enter a first event
data.empty.manual.body: A position is typed as the events that built it — a purchase, its date, its price. If you no longer have the date, record your best estimate.
data.imports.title: Import and export
data.drop.title: Drop a .csv or .xlsx file: you will see what it would do before it writes
data.drop.body: The app reads it by itself, whatever it is called, and shows you the import before recording it.
data.import.duplicates: Write the lines already in my ledger
data.import.preview.title: What this import would do
data.import.preview.body: Nothing has been written yet. Close this window and the file is forgotten.
data.import.file.covers: {count, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} · from {from} to {to} · {symbols, plural, one {# security} other {# securities}}
data.import.file.rows: {count, plural, =0 {no line} one {# line} other {# lines}}
data.import.accounts.title: The accounts
data.import.accounts.settled: {count, plural, one {The account this file names is already declared.} other {The # accounts this file names are already declared.}}
data.import.accounts.why.declaring: “{account}” will be declared with the file
data.import.accounts.dropped: This mapping applies to this import only. The next file will ask again.
data.import.duplicates.title: The duplicates
data.import.duplicates.why: Two purchases of ten shares at the same price on the same day is one order filled twice. You are the only one who knows.
data.import.currency.title: The currency
data.import.currency.offer: This file records its amounts in {currency}, and you have not chosen a base currency yet. Use it? You cannot change it afterwards.
data.import.skipped: {count, plural, =0 {no duplicate skipped} one {# duplicate skipped} other {# duplicates skipped}}
data.import.blocked.one: One correspondence is missing: say where this account's {count, plural, one {# event} other {# events}} go.
data.import.blocked.many: {count} correspondences are missing: every account the file names has to have a target.
data.export.title: Export
data.export.heading: What you are exporting
data.export.events.note: {count, plural, one {# ledger line} other {# ledger lines}}
data.export.workbook.note: A workbook, one sheet per year
data.export.selection.note: {count, plural, one {# line retained} other {# lines retained}}
data.bulk.title: {reduced, select, yes {{count, plural, one {Delete the event} other {Delete the # events}}} other {Delete the reduction}}
data.bulk.confirm.title: {count, plural, one {Delete the event {clauses}?} other {Delete the # events {clauses}?}}
data.bulk.confirm.body: Every event shown leaves the ledger, including the ones that came from a file.
data.bulk.confirm.undo: There is no undo and no bin. Export first if you want a backup.
data.wipe.refused.title: No reduction is active
data.wipe.refused.body: With no filter, this gesture would take the whole ledger. It is not the same gesture: it is called Empty the ledger, and it has a confirmation of its own.
data.wipe.title: Empty the ledger · {count, plural, one {# event} other {# events}}?
data.wipe.body: Every event of yours leaves. The accounts you declared and your settings stay. Nothing is recomputed afterwards: there is nothing left to compute.
installation.fact.unread_environment: {count, plural, one {# environment variable is set but read by nothing} other {# environment variables are set but read by nothing}}: {variables}. Since v5 the settings live in the app — set them on this page. Unset the variables, or acknowledge this notice.
installation.fact.unread_environment.uno: Environment variables are set that this version reads for nothing.
installation.fact.reconstruction_running: History is being rebuilt: {complete, plural, one {# series goes} other {# series go}} back to the first purchase, out of {total, number}. Your performance figures will keep moving until it is done.
The historical reconstruction has not reached every first acquisition.
installation.fact.assumed_base_currency: {events, plural, one {# event} other {# events}} on {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} quoted in {currencies} ({symbols}) were imported before any price was known, so their amounts were taken to be in {base} already. If your broker exported them in the security's own currency, re-export those lines in {base} and import the file again. If they were already in {base}, acknowledge this notice.
Amounts imported from files were taken to be in the base currency.
installation.settings.editable.note: Applied the moment you save, with nothing to restart.
installation.settings.imposed.note: Read when the app starts, and set outside it. Changing one means recreating the container.
installation.settings.imposed.default: not set, the app's own value

installation.settings.unchanged: Nothing had changed, so nothing was saved.
installation.settings.refused: These values were refused. Nothing was saved.
settings.regular_interval.hint: How often prices are refreshed while a market is open.
settings.backfill_interval.hint: How often the app fetches another slice of history.
settings.backfill_delay.hint: Pause between two requests, to go easy on the price source.
settings.backfill_chunk_days.hint: How much history each request brings back.
settings.staleness_horizon.hint: Warn when a price stops moving for this long while its market is open. 0 to never warn.
settings.base_currency.hint: Every figure in the app is shown in this currency.
settings.cadence.reach: Applies now to {now, plural, one {# share} other {# shares}}{later, plural, =0 {} one {, and to # more when its market opens} other {, and to # more when their markets open}}.
settings.backoff.retroactive: A share that cannot be priced waits a multiple of this delay before the next try. Changing it also applies to shares already failing.
settings.jobs.column.name: Workload
settings.jobs.state: {state, select, ok {Running normally.} attention {Something needs a look.} other {Nothing has run yet.}}
settings.jobs.scheduler: The scheduler is stopped. Nothing will run again until the app restarts.
settings.jobs.unfolded: The app could not report on its tasks. Your data is not affected — the logs will say more.
settings.jobs.scrape.verdict: {verdict, select, open {{held, plural, one {# share polled} other {# shares polled}}, markets open.} closed {{held, plural, one {# share held} other {# shares held}}. Markets closed, next pass at the next opening.} frozen {Prices not moving while their market is: {symbols}.} failing {No price could be read for {symbols}.} backoff {{symbols} keep failing and are retried less and less often.} write_failed {A price was read but could not be saved: {symbols}.} other {{held, plural, one {# share held} other {# shares held}}.}}

installation.store.persistence: {state, select, persistent {This path is on a volume that outlives the container.} ephemeral {This path is inside the container and is lost when it is recreated.} other {The app cannot tell whether this path outlives the container.}}
installation.store.ephemeral.title: This container keeps nothing
installation.store.ephemeral.body: The store is inside the container, so everything you record is lost when it is recreated. Fine for trying the app out. To keep your data, mount a volume on this path and restart.
installation.store.size.note: A purge frees rows, not bytes: the store reuses its own blocks, so this figure does not go down.
installation.store.orphans: {count, plural, one {# share nothing declares any more} other {# shares nothing declares any more}}
installation.store.orphans.body: Their prices were kept when their events were deleted: an event can be entered again, a rebuilt history cannot. Positions you have sold are not affected.
problem.storageUnavailable: Your data cannot be read right now. The app is running, but its store is not answering.
problem.notFound: The app answered that this does not exist.
problem.badRequest: The app refused the request this page made.
problem.conflict: Refused: that name already exists, or something still depends on it.
problem.unreplayableLedger: Refused, and nothing changed: the ledger would end up selling shares it does not hold.
problem.unreplayableLedger.write: The app refused and wrote nothing: this sells {wanted, plural, one {{wanted, number, ::.####} share} other {{wanted, number, ::.####} shares}} of {symbol}, and your ledger holds {owned, number, ::.####} of them that day.
problem.unreplayableLedger.remove: The app refused and removed nothing: a later sale of {symbol} rests on this — it sells {wanted, plural, one {{wanted, number, ::.####} share} other {{wanted, number, ::.####} shares}}, and {owned, number, ::.####} would be left.
problem.unreplayableLedger.write.inAccou: The app refused and wrote nothing: this sells {wanted, plural, one {{wanted, number, ::.####} share} other {{wanted, number, ::.####} shares}} of {symbol} out of the {account} account, and that account holds {owned, number, ::.####} of them that day. If these rows belong to another account, it is the account to correct, not the file.
problem.unreplayableLedger.remove.inAcco: The app refused and removed nothing: a later sale of {symbol} in the {account} account rests on this — it sells {wanted, plural, one {{wanted, number, ::.####} share} other {{wanted, number, ::.####} shares}}, and {owned, number, ::.####} would be left.
problem.invalidFile: The app refused this file and wrote nothing. Check that it is an event ledger, that the accounts it names are declared, and that its columns are the ones the export writes.
problem.tooLarge: This file is larger than the app takes in one go. Export a narrower range, or split it.
problem.internal: The app hit an error it did not expect.
problem.unreachable: The app is not answering. Nothing on screen comes from it.
